decisions.reason: Keeping the solenoid and requiring a seamless pour sequence do not change the existing button-controlled valve behavior.
The sealing statement reaffirms the existing requirement to prevent liquid from leaking into the base without changing its state.
The controlled-pour changes do not alter mixing-quality state; the message's separate texture and mixing clauses are already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
Flow without sputtering concerns dispensing rather than mixing splash control, whose separate same-message changes are already represented.
The pour-quality decision does not resolve or otherwise change the independently ambiguous whisk-head design.
The source changes pour behavior but does not change the requirement that the spout face the barista.
The clean pour sequence and absence of sputtering do not change the spout's rendering reference, material, or fabrication method.
The source reiterates removable or easily cleaned spout components, which is already captured by the existing cleaning requirement.
The source does not change the selected stainless-steel food-contact material.
Effective sealing against leakage into the base reaffirms, but does not change, the existing liquid-isolation requirement.
Requesting input before finalizing the BOM does not change the BOM deliverable or component-sourcing strategy.
The dispensing-flow decision has no effect on the prototype's 120V power-input requirement.
